name: Vasovagal syncope
rawContent:
# Vasovagal syncope: Core Condition Reference

## Overview
Vasovagal syncope is transient loss of consciousness from reflex hypotension/bradycardia with rapid spontaneous recovery.

overview.definition: Vasovagal syncope is transient loss of consciousness from reflex hypotension/bradycardia with rapid spontaneous recovery.
overview.epidemiology: Common and usually benign, especially in younger people.
overview.pathophysiology: Autonomic reflex causes peripheral vasodilation and/or bradycardia leading to transient cerebral hypoperfusion.

symptoms: Transient faint with prodrome (nausea, warmth, visual dimming)
atypicalPresentations: Convulsive movements can occur briefly during syncope

firstLine: Glucose and focused blood tests if indicated
secondLine: Ambulatory monitoring/echo when cardiac cause suspected
specialistTests: Tilt-table testing in selected recurrent unexplained cases

diagnosis.criteria: Typical trigger/prodrome with benign examination and normal baseline ECG after exclusion of dangerous causes.

firstLine: Treat injuries and observe until baseline recovered
secondLine: Senior review if red flags or uncertainty

monitoring: Education on counter-pressure manoeuvres and hydration/salt optimisation where appropriate

content.prognosis: Generally excellent when cardiac causes are excluded.
content.foundationDoctorRole: Differentiate benign reflex syncope from high-risk causes using history, ECG and red-flag screening.
content.escalation: Escalate for abnormal ECG, exertional syncope, chest pain, dyspnoea, persistent altered state, or recurrent unexplained episodes.
content.keySafetyConsiderations: Never label as vasovagal until serious cardiac/neurological causes are considered.
